nodes.label: Toward Evaluation Frameworks for Multi-Agent Scientific AI Systems
nodes.author: Marcin Abram
nodes.rationale: Analyzes challenges of benchmarking scientific multi-agentic systems including contamination risks, ground truth problems, tool use complications, and proposes evaluation strategies for open-ended reasoning.

nodes.label: Scientific Multi-Agent AI System
nodes.rationale: Integrates LLMs with external tools, simulation capabilities, and iterative reasoning for physics research assistance; architecture includes data, orchestration, interaction, and validation layers.

nodes.label: Data Contamination Problem
nodes.rationale: Core benchmarking challenge: LLM cutoff insufficient; information distributed across Reddit, lectures, transcripts; requires restricting to novel problems or masking identifying information.

nodes.label: Retrieval vs. Reasoning Distinction
nodes.rationale: Key challenge: well-designed systems should use retrieval when appropriate; benchmarks must distinguish genuine reasoning from retrieval and synthesis.

nodes.label: Ground Truth Problem for Novel Research
nodes.rationale: Dilemma: known problems enable verification but contaminate via retrieval; novel problems lack ground truth; solution: programmatically-generated problems hard to solve but easy to verify.

nodes.label: Planted-Structure Problems
nodes.rationale: Contamination-resistant problem class where answer is engineered; enables verification while avoiding retrieval shortcuts.

nodes.label: Constraint-Modified Problems
nodes.rationale: Non-standard modifications of original problems render straightforward lookup futile; maintains difficulty while preventing retrieval contamination.

nodes.label: MMLU Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Early LLM evaluation: 57-subject closed-form questions; privileges recall over open-ended reasoning; frontier models approaching saturation.

nodes.label: GPQA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Graduate-level physics/biology/chemistry questions intentionally 'Google-proof'; frontier models exceed 90% on Diamond subset, signaling need for harder tests.

nodes.label: PaperBench Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluates AI agents on ICML 2024 paper replication; 8,316 individually gradable sub-tasks; best agent achieves 21.0% vs 41.4% human PhD baseline.

nodes.label: ReplicationBench Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Astrophysics paper-scale tasks measuring faithfulness and correctness; frontier models score below 20%; reveals rich taxonomy of error modes.

nodes.label: AI Scientist System
nodes.rationale: End-to-end autonomous scientific discovery pipeline: hypothesis generation, code execution, paper production; v2 removes human templates, produces first AI-generated workshop paper passing peer review.

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Interaction Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Benchmarks should capture iterative scientific workflows: literature consultation, approach revision, colleague feedback; more realistic than single-shot question-answer.

nodes.label: Uncertainty Calibration
nodes.rationale: Evaluation dimension: does system know when it does not know? Critical for high-stakes scientific applications.

nodes.label: Tool Selection Capability
nodes.rationale: Evaluation dimension for multi-agent systems: ability to choose appropriate tools for given problems.

nodes.label: Reasoning Process Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Evaluation dimension: validity of intermediate steps, not just final result; critical for scientific reasoning assessment.

nodes.label: Point Tests (Unit Tests)
nodes.rationale: Evaluation level: unit tests for specific tools or subsystems in multi-agent architecture.

nodes.label: Integration Tests
nodes.rationale: Evaluation level: pipelines chaining multiple subsystems (e.g., literature search → simulation → interpretation).

nodes.label: End-to-End Task Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Evaluation level: question in, answer out; measures overall system performance on complete tasks.

nodes.label: UX and User Interaction Tests
nodes.rationale: Evaluation level: coherence of multi-turn conversations, ability to push back on incorrect ideas, realistic uncertainty calibration.

nodes.label: Operational Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Evaluation level: latency, resource usage, failure rates; practical deployment considerations.

nodes.label: Difficulty Scaling via Continuous Parameter
nodes.rationale: Benchmark design principle: enables scaling curves revealing breaking points; more informative than single accuracy value.

nodes.label: Multi-Dimensional Scoring
nodes.rationale: Evaluation principle: open-ended problems require multiple dimensions (mathematical correctness, physical plausibility, logical clarity, novelty, specificity, limitations).

nodes.label: Automatic Verification
nodes.rationale: Benchmark design principle: results should be automatically checkable; numerical results vs known values, analytical derivations via proof tooling.

nodes.label: Benchmark Taxonomy for Scientific AI Systems
nodes.rationale: Organizes benchmark families for evaluating agentic scientific AI systems across replication, error detection, scientific reasoning, and discovery tasks

nodes.label: Replication Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Leverages hidden knowledge gap in papers to test whether systems can reproduce derivations and numerical results using only published information

nodes.label: Error Detection Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Tests ability to find mistakes or validate calculations by introducing errors into papers and measuring detection capability

nodes.label: Scientific Reasoning Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Evaluates reasoning capabilities through future research directions prediction, counterexample construction, and technique recommendation

nodes.label: Discovery-Style Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Tests creative scientific work through fabricated phenomena explanation and novel problem solving

nodes.label: Planted-Structure Problems
nodes.rationale: Construction strategy that creates original problems with known answers to avoid data contamination and retrieval shortcuts

nodes.label: Constraint-Modified Problems
nodes.rationale: Introduces non-standard constraints into familiar problems to force reasoning about specific structure rather than retrieval

nodes.label: Dynamic Difficulty Families
nodes.rationale: Designs problem families with difficulty parameters to obtain scaling curves revealing performance degradation points

nodes.label: Self-Consistency Tests
nodes.rationale: Tests internal consistency of outputs without ground truth by solving problems using different approaches

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Scientific Dialogue
nodes.rationale: Engages system in progressive information revelation to test question-asking ability and adaptive reasoning

nodes.label: System Evaluation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Multi-faced evaluation approach including ablation studies, tool-use analysis, process-level evaluation, and scaling curves

nodes.label: Human-Centered Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Incorporates user interviews and sentiment analysis to align benchmarks with actual researcher and engineer needs

nodes.label: Future Research Directions Extraction
nodes.rationale: Feasibility study demonstrating extraction of 414 future directions from 300 papers using LLM-based pipeline

nodes.label: Benchmark Design for Scientific AI Systems
nodes.rationale: Unified framework for evaluating agentic scientific systems across multiple benchmark families and construction strategies
